description: We're a passionate group of students who are excited to collaborate and build an innovative solution for this year’s NASA Space Apps Challenge! Our team consists of Supreet, Charmi, Ambreen, and Amy. We're space enthusiasts, who love to innovate, and think outside the box while creating solutions.
summary:
The goal of this challenge was to create an engaging, story-driven educational tool or narrative that teaches school-age and casual space enthusiasts about the hardware left on the Moon, Mars, and elsewhere. Our solution was to build an interactive, narrative-driven game that's dopamin-driven, teaching school aged children and casual enthusiasts about the history and significance of space artifacts left behind? 


Our visual novel follows you, a human that has been exiled from Earth and is only allowed back once you have collected the required amount of artifacts. The objective of the game is to explore the Moon and Mars for artifacts left behind, learning about their impact and importance along the way. From aliens attacking to escaping Mars with the help of rovers like Perseverance, 'Operation: Adventuring for Artifacts' is filled with extraterrestrial adventures and tons of information about space relics. 


Your objective is to collect each artifact, read about its history, fight aliens, and complete stellar missions! From this engaging game, you can learn about why NASA leaves debris and hardware on the Moon and Mars, all while having a blast.
details:
Our project is story-driven educational tool which effectively teaches the player about hardware left in space during various missions and the science it made possible. By playing our game, not only do they learn about why people leave hardware in space, but they also get an the opportunity to see, and learn about examples of missions, and the specific types of items left in space. For people with short attention spans, we have lots of visuals as well as games, which everyone will enjoy for sure. From Apollo 11 moon mission to the Mars Pathfinder and the abandoning of Sojourner robotic rover, our game has it all. Our game works by keyboard controls, such as space bar, and the arrow keys. Operation: Adventuring for Artifacts has a wide range of benefits, as it spreads awareness about items and hardware left in space, and allows people to have fun at the same time. In order to create our game, we first wrote the storyline, in which we divided into interesting 6 chapters with clear instructions to play the game. Then, we used base 44 to turn our project into a visually appealing, and interactive game. Our project is creative, because it combines aspects of storytelling with a unique game component, and a small quiz in the end. Our game is perfect for those who have a knack for reading, gaming, and problem solving. It's also perfect for those who don't have much background knowledge, but are willing to learn from the experience. Our team considers various factors, such as player experience (we had to ensure that our game was adequate for those who have background knowledge, and those who don't), attention span (we know that people have short attention spans, which is why we combined various aspects-like stories, games, quizzes, etc), and the most important factor, we want the player(s) to have fun all while learning something new!

Here is everything explained chapter by chapter:

Chapter 1:

In chapter 1, we started off with an interesting message, which engages the player into actually playing our game with enthusiasm.

Elaborating On Game Writeup:

Imagine stepping foot on the Moon, expecting perpetual darkness with the Earth glowing from a distance. Feeling the lunar dirt under your lunar overboot, walking on craters, and walking in front of a flag? Golf balls? Or a family photograph? What if we told you there were many extraterrestrial stories untold behind the groundbreaking science which paved the way for today's achievements and tomorrow’s exploration.

Chapter 2:

In chapter 2, we gave the player an artifact list, and told them their objective, which was to explore the debris sites, and collect artifacts, all while shooting the aliens.

Elaborating On Game Writeup:

You’ve been exiled from Earth because of your own wrongdoings… Not a normal kind of exile. You are permitted to return back to Earth, as long as you fulfill the requirements of obtaining 16 of the artifacts on the lists, 12 from the Moon, and 4 from Mars. Your objective is to explore the Moon for artifacts left behind, with a twist. From aliens attacking to escaping Mars with the help of rovers like Perseverance, this engaging game is filled with extraterrestrial adventures you must take on to be successful.

 

The player's objective is to explore these debris sites and collect the 12 required artifacts left behind, but escape from the aliens attacking you from above!

Chapter 3:

In chapter 3, we start of by showing a short clip of a spaceship travelling to mars, and then a message pops up saying:

"You have finally reached Mars with your 10 items after battling the aliens."

Then we state that Olympus Mons starts erupting, and you must complete your mission, by choosing an efficient rover and collecting the designated number of artifacts:

Elaborating On Game Writeup:

Oh no! After millions of years, the Olympus Mons, which is the biggest volcano in our solar system, has finally erupted. You are in great danger, and you must complete your mission quickly. To complete this mission, you shall find a rover that works efficiently so you can travel on Mars. After finding the rover, you need to find four more artifacts on this red planet. You shall move swiftly, or else you will be engulfed in lava. 

Chapter 4:

In chapter 4, we explain why artifacts are left in space in the first place by various examples. To further elaborate on this, we have also included the footage of the Apollo 11 ascent-stage launch so that the players have a visual interpretation of our explanation. We have also included a mini quiz in the end with 5 questions, if you get a question wrong, it's okay, because you get to learn from the experience, and understand the correct answer and the reasoning behind it from the game.

Elaborating On Game Writeup:

But why were these artifacts left in space? Imagine, every time you played soccer, you had this innate sensation telling you to leave your shin guards on the soccer field to leave your mark on the ground. To leave behind a legacy that is yours. NASA has done this too in their own way, because of both scientific and emotional factors. If up to physics, the less mass you have, the faster and easier it is for you to manoeuvre. Imagine you were the men inside Apollo 11, unaware of the human-sized craters on the lunar surface, as they were too tiny to have been predicted with all the available equipment in 1969. 

At the hellbent speed you’re going, you could reach from one side of a college campus to the other in only a couple mere seconds. One minute is all you have left to land safely on the Moon, or else the spacecraft would tip over, and you would be reduced to cinders. Now imagine instead of one minute, you had 30 seconds. The time you have to find relatively smooth land on the Moon before you get engulfed in flames, cut in half. That could be avoided if you had just a little bit less mass on your spacecraft. 

NASA leaves debris and hardware on Mars because every part added to the landing system adds weight, and carrying extra material is scientifically unnecessary, as well as expensive. Fun fact! Rovers like Curiosity, Perseverance, and Spirit are designed as one-way science trips. There’s no return stage, or rocket ship built into them to pack up their discarded landing gear. Many of you may wonder: how do spaceships discard all this stuff, and what stuff do they typically discard? Well, spaceships discard heavy heat shields, backshells, sky cranes, and supersonic parachutes mid-air once they have slowed the rover down. All these pieces crash-land at a safe distance, far away from the rover.

We included a fun fact blurb about the exploration rovers on Mars such as Spirit and Opportunity.

Fun Fact Summary:

Chapter 5:

In chapter 5, we have a message showing the player that they're successful, and they've made it back to Earth.

Chapter 6: The Return

In chapter 6, we left the player on a cliffhanger, so they're interested in playing the next game we release!

Elaborating On Game Writeup:

As soon as you start living your beautiful, healthy life, disaster strikes. The aliens are back, and they’ve hunted you down. Defeat is not an option. Success is improbable. The story will continue in Operation Adventuring for Artifacts: The Return.
